subject: Post-period makegood and capacity amendment
messages:
From: Samantha Park <samantha@stormline.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-period capacity overage and makegood

Hi Olga,

We just finished our internal audit for April and discovered significant overage relative to our committed capacity — roughly 230k additional inference minutes that weren't accounted for under our plan. Our accounting team asked me to reach out to get a reconciliation and a proposal for one-time settlement or an alternative amortization.

Attached is our raw usage export (stormline_usage_april.csv). Can you confirm whether this matches Redwood's server-side logs and share an estimate for the settlement amount? We also want to discuss whether bumping committed capacity for the rest of the term would prevent a repeat.

Samantha Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Stormline
samantha@stormline.io
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: stormline_usage_april.csv (CSV, 82KB)
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@stormline.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-period capacity overage and makegood

Hi Samantha — thanks for the upload, and sorry for the surprise. I pulled a quick pass against our ingest logs and there is indeed an April spike that aligns with the rows in your CSV.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll run the official reconciliation against our billing logs and produce a simple statement of amounts (one-time charge vs amortized).
- Ben (cc'd) can advise on capacity amendment options mid-term.
- Laura (cc'd) will confirm invoicing cadence and whether we can push a partial credit.

I’ve attached a draft calc (Stormline_trueup_calc_v1.xlsx) with two scenarios: one-time invoice and a 3-month amortization. Rough preliminary numbers indicate a gross settlement in the ~$18k–$20k range before any discretionary credit. I’ll aim to have a finalized figure by EOD Friday if that works for you. Can we do a 30-min call tomorrow to align on approach?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
+1 650-555-0199

Attachment: Stormline_trueup_calc_v1.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-period capacity overage and makegood

All — quick internal note on options:

1) One-time settlement: invoice for the full amount (we estimate $18,450). Clean and quick.
2) Amortize over 3 months: invoice $6,150/mo (preferred by some mid-market finance teams).
3) Partial credit + short invoice: marketing/CS discretionary credit up to $2,500 to maintain goodwill, invoice remainder.

Operationally, if Stormline is open to a capacity amendment, we can lock them into an increased committed tier starting next billing period to avoid repeat. For today, I suggest we offer option 3 (credit + invoice remainder) in our external message and include a clear doc covering the revised capacity going forward.

Also — if they need a PO number for the invoice, let us know and we’ll route to finance with that PO on file.

-Ben
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-period capacity overage and makegood

Ben — agree with option 3. From an account perspective, Stormline is in expansion talks and a small concession is the right trade-off to keep momentum.

If Finance is good with a $2,500 courtesy credit, we can propose:
- Credit: $2,500 (applied to next invoice)
- Invoice: $15,950 one-time (or spread across 3 months at $5,317/mo)
- Signed addendum to increase committed capacity by 20% starting next billing cycle (term amendment).

Laura — can you draft the invoice with the credit line and the payment terms (Net 30)? Also flag this for PO processing if Stormline sends a PO.

Rishi
Senior Customer Success Manager
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-period capacity overage and makegood

Thanks — I can do that. I’ll prepare a formal settlement statement and invoice and include the $2,500 credit line as discussed. Draft will be attached as settlement_statement.pdf. Payment terms Net 30; please confirm the billing contact/PO once Stormline responds.

I’ll also add a note for deferred revenue impact (this will be recognized at invoice).

Laura Bennett
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@stormline.io>, Paulo Mendes <paulo@stormline.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Accounting <ar@stormline.io>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Final proposal: settlement + capacity amendment (Stormline)

Hi Samantha / Paulo — thanks for the patience while we reconciled. Below is our agreed proposal (internal discussions summarized):

Proposal:
- Gross overage amount (April): $18,450
- Courtesy credit: $2,500
- Net due: $15,950
- Option A (preferred): one-time invoice for $15,950, Net 30
- Option B: amortize across 3 months at $5,317/mo (Net 30 each)

Capacity amendment:
- Increase committed inference capacity by 20% starting next billing cycle; term amendment/addendum will be provided for signature.

Next actions:
1) If you approve Option A, Laura will issue the one-time invoice and attach the settlement_statement.pdf.
2) If you prefer Option B, reply with preferred amortization and we’ll issue installment invoices.
3) Please confirm PO number (if required) so Finance can process quickly.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/Stormline-Trueup-Envelope
Drive: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b-stormline-trueup

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out and getting the capacity bump in place.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
